method: Source-only comparison; no tests or applications executed.

entries.title: Executable identity, stock launcher and Bun bootstrap ordering
entries.what: Starting Ice establishes its process identity and runtime adapters before invoking the main command. The distribution has separate Node/source and compiled Bun launch paths, whose ordering affects provider availability and inherited environment state.
entries.mechanism:
Each executable establishes process identity before handing control to the main application. The Bun build also installs runtime-specific provider adapters and repairs only a completely empty environment.

The stock cli.ts imports legacy bootstrap before main, sets process.title to APP_NAME, assigns ICE_CODING_AGENT='true' and AI_AGENT='ice', replaces process.emitWarning with a no-op, configures the global HTTP dispatcher, then calls main(process.argv.slice(2)) without a top-level await. The bootstrap module itself only assigns ICE_CODING_AGENT; it does not translate historical environment names (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli.ts:1-21; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/legacy-compat/bootstrap.ts:1-5).

The Bun launcher first sets title and suppresses process warnings, registers Bun OAuth flows, invokes restoreSandboxEnv, awaits registration of the injected Bun Bedrock adapter, and only then dynamically imports the ICE distribution entrypoint. The Bedrock registration calls setInjectedBedrockModule with the Bun module; provider implementation remains AI/AUTH ownership (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/bun/cli.ts:1-15; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/bun/register-bedrock.ts:1-4).

restoreSandboxEnv is a narrowly gated workaround: return unless process.versions.bun is truthy and Object.keys(process.env).length is zero. Otherwise read /proc/self/environ as UTF-8, split NUL records, take the first '=' only when its index is positive, and assign each exact name/value into process.env. All read failures are ignored. There is no explicit platform check; unavailable /proc is handled by that catch. The candidate called an indexed environment read at line 30 is actually an assignment. Existing source tests cover non-Bun, already-populated environment and successful NUL restoration; they were read, not executed (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/bun/restore-sandbox-env.ts:17-36; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/restore-sandbox-env.test.ts:11-77).
entries.interfaces: Stock executable passes argv excluding executable/script to main. Process markers are ICE_CODING_AGENT='true' and AI_AGENT='ice'; title uses APP_NAME. Bun restoration changes only a completely empty process.env and does not fill missing names in a nonempty map. The raw /proc path is an input to the TS workaround, not a required persistent file.
entries.dependency_text: CLI-002 owns the ICE distribution wrapper. CLI-018 owns exact-name compatibility helpers. AI-003 and AUTH-012/015 own provider dispatch, Bedrock credentials and generic OAuth registration. SET-013 owns the HTTP dispatcher algorithm; this entry owns invocation order.
entries.rust: The native binary uses a multi-thread Tokio runtime, awaits app::run and converts its integer code to ExitCode through a u8 cast; lib.rs supplies HOST_NAME/HOST_VERSION. It has no JavaScript warning hook, Bun injection layer or empty-process.env bug to reproduce (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/bin/ice.rs:1-21; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/lib.rs:82-89). Full app.rs startup and a scoped crates search found no corresponding assignments for ICE_CODING_AGENT/AI_AGENT, or PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR launcher bridge. The environment configuration name ICE_CODING_AGENT_DIR does exist and must not be confused with the ICE_CODING_AGENT marker (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:82-190; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:89-108).
entries.port: Keep native startup/runtime construction. Add the documented process markers before provider/extension initialization if compatibility consumers require them, and define the native process-title equivalent explicitly. Do not copy JS-only warning suppression or the Bun /proc workaround into ordinary Rust environment handling. Verify the stock/distribution entrypoint distinction and adapter registration order in future implementation checks; this audit executed neither entrypoint.
entries.priority_reason: Launch identity is a small compatibility boundary; Bun-specific workarounds should remain runtime-specific rather than inflate the native gap.

entries.title: ICE distribution preflight, early agent commands and builtin factory order
entries.what: The ICE launcher adds guarded distribution behavior before the reusable coding-agent main function runs. Its early command handling and factory installation determine which policies and integrations are available to later startup.
entries.mechanism:
The distribution launcher handles a few commands before normal startup and installs its policy integrations in a fixed order. Its callbacks keep the parent session and current mode live as the runtime changes.

ice.ts sets ICE_CODING_AGENT, AI_AGENT and process title, fills PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR with getAgentDir only when the existing value is nullish, suppresses process warnings and configures the HTTP dispatcher. An existing empty PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR is preserved. It scans raw arguments for exact --import-agent-pack or the '=...' spelling anywhere in argv. More than one occurrence errors and exits 1. The single source is the inline suffix or following token; empty or leading-dash source errors. Successful import targets the global agent definitions directory, prints its summary and exits 0; failure prints its message and exits 1. This occurs before normal flag parsing and before the agents subcommand (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice.ts:24-57).

When argv[0] is 'agents', runAgentsCli receives the remaining arguments, current cwd, agent directory and stdout writer, and its returned code becomes process exit. Otherwise normalizeUnsafeSubagentStartupArgs receives strict stdin/stdout isTTY===true, then validateIceStartupArgs runs; validation errors print and exit 1. The normalized arguments then determine offline and metadata-only flags. refreshLocalModelsForStartup is awaited with skip/onFailure options before runtime factories are constructed; AUTH-032 records that the current helper does not actually perform the implied remote refresh (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice.ts:59-86).

The wrapper creates one AgentViewBridge and one safe-verify factory whose change callbacks update local mode/capability variables. It awaits main with globalFirstSettings=true and hidden builtin factories in this order: safe verify, provider settings, Cognee, subagents. The subagent factory registers the MCP adapter using a live getParentSession callback, installs session_shutdown unregistration, then binds subagent hooks, bridge and live mode/capability getters. This ordering precedes user extension factories through main's builtin factory composition (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/ice.ts:88-130; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:530-532).
entries.interfaces: Early raw surfaces: --import-agent-pack <source>, --import-agent-pack=<source>, and 'ice agents ...'. Compatibility marker PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR uses nullish assignment. Distribution policy flags are normalized/validated before main; their authority semantics belong to SUB. main receives extensionFactories plus globalFirstSettings and agentViewBridge rather than a separate application implementation.
entries.dependency_text: SUB owns agent definitions, guarded mode/authority policy, agent view bridge and extension lifecycle. AUTH-028 owns provider settings/catalog submenu behavior, AUTH-032 the actual startup model helper, EXT-002 exact historical package imports. Cognee/MCP mechanisms require their owning area links; this entry owns only installation/order and live callbacks.
entries.rust: Native startup has substantial early dispatch of its own: hidden dev cleanup, --connect, offline normalization, dev/dev-local wrapping, and auth/events/update/install/uninstall/package commands. Historical pi-package/pi-update/install-pi/uninstall-pi names are explicitly rejected with usage code 2 (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:82-172). That dispatch is not the TS ICE agents/import-pack/preflight/factory stack. Native extensions and package integrations may supply related capabilities, but the inspected app startup does not install these four TS distribution factories or expose the same raw command routes. The --connect assignment line 96 is connector-redacted and is not reconstructed.
entries.port: Add an explicit distribution startup layer around the existing native app, preserving native commands while implementing the authorized agents/import-pack routing and policy normalization through SUB-owned components. Install runtime integrations in deterministic order with live bridge/mode getters and matching shutdown unregistration. Decide the PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR bridge only at the actual package boundary, without treating it as permission to load arbitrary legacy modules or read historical user state.
entries.priority_reason: Distribution policy and subagent integrations must be installed before user extensions and session execution; a parser-only port does not provide this behavior.

entries.title: Argument token grammar, complete flag surface and diagnostic semantics
entries.what: The command parser separates messages, file arguments, known settings and extension flags in one ordered pass. Small token-consumption differences change which prompt or option reaches the application, even when both implementations recognize most flag names.
entries.mechanism:
The parser walks arguments once and decides whether each token is a known option, extension flag, file or message. Repeated options, missing values and flag-like prompt text follow precise rules that affect the resulting request.

TS initializes ordered messages/fileArgs/diagnostics arrays and an insertion-ordered unknownFlags Map. Scalar repeats use the last value; append-system-prompt, extension, skill, prompt-template and theme append in encounter order. Known value flags normally require only that another token exists and consume it even when it begins '-' or '@'; special --name and --ui-mode branches add their own errors. A missing ordinary long value flag falls through to unknown-long handling, while a missing recognized short value spelling becomes an unknown-short error. Known '=value' spellings are not generally recognized: except --observe=, they enter unknownFlags under the stripped name (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/args.ts:69-247).

The boolean/action surface is --help/-h, --version/-v, --print-system-template, --observe, --continue/-c, --resume/-r, --no-session, --no-tools/-nt, --no-builtin-tools/-nbt, --fast, --no-fast, --print/-p, --no-extensions/-ne, --no-skills/-ns, --no-prompt-templates/-np, --no-themes, --no-context-files/-nc, --verbose, --approve/-a, --no-approve/-na and --offline. Value surfaces are --mode, --provider, --model, --api-key, --system-prompt, repeated --append-system-prompt, --name/-n, --session, --session-id, --fork, --session-dir, --models, --tools/-t, --exclude-tools/-xt, --thinking, --export, repeated --extension/-e, --skill, --prompt-template, --theme, optional --list-models and --ui-mode (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/args.ts:80-221).

--mode consumes its next token but assigns only text/json/rpc; invalid values are silently ignored. --thinking accepts exactly off/minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max/ultra; invalid values add a warning and leave a prior valid value intact. --models splits commas and trims but retains empty entries; tools/exclude-tools remove empty entries. --observe= converts using Number and requires an integer 1..65535; bare --observe is true and consumes no port token. --ui-mode accepts exact regular/fullscreen; missing or leading-dash value errors without consuming the next flag, while an invalid ordinary value is consumed and reported (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/args.ts:63-67; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/args.ts:86-100; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/args.ts:133-168; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/args.ts:194-213).

-p may consume the following prompt unless it begins '@' or begins '-' without the special '---' prefix. That prefix deliberately accepts YAML frontmatter. Optional --list-models consumes only a following non-flag/non-file token. Any token starting '@' becomes fileArgs with its first character removed, including bare '@' becoming an empty path. Unknown long flags support '--name=value', or consume one following non-flag/non-file string, otherwise true. Bare '--' is therefore an unknown flag with an empty name, not an end-of-options marker. Every other leading '-' token, including bare '-', reports an error. Existing tests cover representative aliases, repeatable options, tool flags, unknown flags and YAML prompts; they do not establish every boundary listed here by execution (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/args.ts:163-247; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/args.test.ts:36-61; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/args.test.ts:411-466).
entries.interfaces: parseArgs(string[])→Args with diagnostics [{type:'warning'|'error',message}], unknownFlags Map<string,string|boolean>, ordered messages/fileArgs and optional settings. Main reports warnings and errors separately; credential-print treats any diagnostic as command failure. Exact field consumers are CLI-004/006/007/011/017/019.
entries.dependency_text: AI-005 owns thinking-level clamp behavior after parsing, SET-003 project trust policy. Parser acceptance alone does not implement service-tier, dashboard, resource or model behavior.
entries.rust: Native args.rs genuinely parses most common flags and has extensive inline tests. It additionally recognizes --base-url, --timeout, --extensions-dir/ICE_EXTENSIONS_DIR, --dev-local-only, --project-only and --debug-system-prompt. It peels '=value' for all long flags; take_value rejects a following dash-prefixed value except bare '-'. It stores unknown flags in a sorted BTreeMap; CSV values drop empty fields; theme is a last-wins scalar; --thinking lacks ultra; invalid --mode is a usage error. Native --tui-mode accepts case-insensitive regular/fullscreen and defaults to regular on macOS, fullscreen elsewhere, while TS's public flag is --ui-mode. It does not recognize fast/no-fast/observe/print-system-template as builtins. Bare '@' and '-' become messages in Rust. The -p branch lacks the TS '---' prompt exception (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/args.rs:76-270; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/args.rs:271-555; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/args.rs:718-1120).
entries.port: Build an explicit compatibility table for every public spelling and token-consumption rule, retaining native-only flags as documented additions. Implement ultra, fast/no-fast, observe, print-system-template and --ui-mode routing through their owners. Preserve the YAML prompt case and ordered repeated values. Where TS behavior is surprising—missing values, unknown empty '--', empty @ path—document and consciously choose compatibility or a diagnosed correction instead of silently changing semantics. Future verification should cover token boundaries and precedence, not merely recognized names.
entries.priority_reason: Incorrect token consumption can discard a user prompt or reinterpret options; missing flag names are only part of the actual parser gap.

entries.title: Run-mode resolution and metadata short-circuit precedence
entries.what: Startup chooses interactive, print, JSON or RPC behavior and decides how early metadata requests may exit. These choices also determine which errors are reported and which services or migrations have already run.
entries.mechanism:
Mode selection determines who owns the terminal streams and whether startup may run without a model. Metadata commands exit at different stages, so their error precedence and side effects must be tracked separately.

TS resolveAppMode chooses explicit rpc first, explicit json second, then print when -p is set or either stdin or stdout is not a TTY; otherwise interactive. Explicit --mode text alone does not force print on two TTYs. A plain runtime metadata command is exactly !print && mode===undefined && (help || listModels!==undefined); this separate predicate controls stdout takeover. envTruthy recognizes '1' or case-insensitive true/yes without trimming (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:91-115).

Main routes package commands, config command and credential-print before normal parse. It reports all parser diagnostics and exits 1 on any error before --version. Version then prints VERSION alone and exits 0; print-system-template writes DEFAULT_BASE_TEMPLATE plus one newline and exits 0; export uses parsed.export and the first positional output name, reporting an export error and exiting 1 or printing the resulting path and exiting 0. These precede mode selection, session option validation and startup migrations. Thus --version wins over --help after valid parsing, but does not suppress a parse error (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:554-617).

Help and list-models are deliberately later: they select an in-memory session, run migrations and create the runtime/services/extensions, then print extension-aware help or available models before ordinary runtime error diagnostics are reported. Help receives extension flag registrations from the built runtime. A list-models failure can still reject through its awaited helper; model-list success exits 0. RPC rejects CLI file arguments before migrations and never drains piped stdin. After runtime creation, non-RPC piped content can downgrade interactive to print. Noninteractive execution without a resolved model is fatal after runtime diagnostics; the startup benchmark additionally requires interactive mode (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:620-627; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:831-895).
entries.interfaces: App modes are interactive/print/json/rpc. --mode text is the text output selection when print mode is otherwise chosen. TS normal startup usage/runtime errors mostly exit 1; successful metadata paths exit 0. --print-system-template exposes the actual base template, not the expanded per-session system prompt. HTML export implementation is a MISC dependency.
entries.dependency_text: RPC-016 owns the JSONL command-mode protocol boundary, while this entry owns its selection. CLI-005 owns runtime creation and CLI-019 stream routing/cleanup. Model resolution is AUTH-026.
entries.rust: Native handle_parse_short_circuits checks help first, version second and parser errors third, so --help suppresses errors and beats --version. Native version prints 'ice VERSION'; its help is static and does not create services or list extension flags. It migrates its layout after cwd resolution, then handles export and list-models before provider credentials, resume and harness construction (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:174-219; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:523-579; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/args.rs:589-716). Native resolve_mode gives the presence of unknown flag 'server' highest priority, then rpc/json, then -p/non-TTY; later ICE_FORCE_TUI='1' can override it until a plugin stdio claim authoritatively forces RPC. A genuine JSONL branch exists; comments claiming no built-in RPC are stale (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/args.rs:556-578; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:234-235; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:352-381; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:434-505).
entries.port: Define and implement explicit short-circuit precedence for compatibility, including diagnostics before version and extension-aware help, while preserving the native server/stdio ownership path. Add --print-system-template as a real early output route. Keep list-models independent of authenticated prompt execution when adopting the native convenience, and document that deliberate difference if retained. Do not infer resource-free TS help from the flag name; match or consciously simplify its actual service side effects.
entries.priority_reason: Metadata and mode precedence affect scripts, startup side effects and protocol ownership; stale comments currently obscure implemented native behavior.

entries.title: Cwd-bound runtime factory, trust staging and startup service composition
entries.what: CLI startup builds services around the selected session's working directory and repeats that construction when the runtime changes session context. Trust resolution and settings must occur at the correct stage so the session receives the intended resources, model and tool policy.
entries.mechanism:
Startup first resolves the session, then builds settings and resources for that session's working directory. The same factory can rebuild services for a later session replacement while retaining the intended trust and explicit-path boundaries.

Main starts with launch cwd/agent dir and a bootstrap SettingsManager using projectTrusted=false plus the caller's globalFirst option, applies its global HTTP proxy and configures the dispatcher before early package/config/auth routes. After parsing and session-option validation it runs all startup migrations, creates startup settings, drains their errors, optionally performs first setup and resolves the session manager. A requested session name is trimmed, validated and appended before model/runtime validation. Missing stored cwd is handled before the session cwd becomes the runtime construction cwd (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:530-558; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:628-676).

The reusable runtime factory receives a session manager and sessionStartEvent. It caches project trust by cwd, uses explicit overrides first, and detects whether project resources require a trust decision. When a decision is still required it initially creates settings with projectTrusted=false and installs a resource-loader resolveProjectTrust callback. That callback evaluates the current factory cwd with startup global defaultProjectTrust and either the supplied extension context or a CLI context whose metadata-command prompt mode is print. Its result is cached for subsequent construction. When no decision is required, the trusted value comes from cache, explicit override, absence of trust-requiring resources or a stored true decision. Exact policy and parent-folder matching remain SET-003; this is the call order and cache boundary (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:677-747).

Explicit extension/skill/prompt/theme paths resolve once against the original launch cwd, even if a stored session changes cwd; local paths are normalized and package source strings remain package sources. Each factory call constructs cwd-bound settings and services, supplies parsed unknown extension flags, a 15-second model-runtime signal, all explicit/no-resource overrides, system/append prompt and ordered factories. Diagnostics combine trust, service, settings-read and extension-load errors. Scoped model patterns are CLI models if defined, otherwise settings enabled models, resolved with a separate 15-second signal. The factory builds model/tool options, applies a truthy CLI API key only after a provider/model has been selected, creates the agent session, and persists explicit or shorthand thinking by calling setThinkingLevel on the actual created level (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:508-510; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:690-831).

createAgentSessionRuntime owns replacement around this factory. The AgentViewBridge is attached to runtime.session after creation, and the resulting runtime's global proxy/idle timeout are applied before metadata or mode execution. The 15-second signals bound model operations, not every synchronous migration, extension hook or entire startup (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:834-852).
entries.interfaces: main(args,{extensionFactories?,globalFirstSettings?,agentViewBridge?}) composes a runtime factory receiving SessionManager plus optional lifecycle context. Runtime diagnostics remain values until the mode/metadata branch decides to report them. Trust cache keys and service cwd use the selected session cwd; explicit path arguments use launch cwd. CLI-006/007 specify selection and model option precedence.
entries.dependency_text: SESSION-021/028/035 own replaceable runtime, SDK construction and reload sequencing. SET owns settings storage/trust policy, AUTH owns model matching/initial defaults, EXT owns extension binding/resource attribution. This entry does not duplicate those mechanisms.
entries.rust: Native app prepares extensions once before provider resolution, builds authenticated catalog and persists its --models scope, then calls build_prepared. The prepared extension action host is initially unbound; build_prepared installs the catalog, cwd-bound OsExecutionEnv/tool context, merged tool policy, selected session and identity before prompt/harness creation. It is real composition, not absent SDK functionality (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:246-313; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/session.rs:209-240; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/session.rs:345-466). However startup uses process cwd, direct resolve_project_trust and native reload context; it does not implement the TS factory's per-session cwd trust cache, startup diagnostic value list, launch-relative explicit paths, global-first option or typed runtime replacement flow. Native missing-cwd restore warns rather than using TS interactive approval/headless failure (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/session.rs:2676-2713).
entries.port: Reuse prepared native extensions and harness assembly behind a cwd-aware runtime factory. Connect trust and settings before loading project resources, keep launch-relative explicit paths stable across restored cwd changes, and give replacement operations a single owner through SESSION-021. Preserve typed startup diagnostics and model-operation deadlines. Ensure migration order and requested-name timing are deliberate; permission policy must not be inferred from a successfully constructed settings object.
entries.priority_reason: Startup service composition determines which project code and policy enter a session; wrong cwd or trust staging creates functional and authority mismatches.

entries.title: Startup session selection, exact-ID validation, naming and missing-cwd recovery
entries.what: Session flags select the conversation before the runtime is created, and some combinations are rejected rather than silently prioritized. Opening a different project or a session whose cwd disappeared has distinct confirmation, failure and persistence behavior.
entries.mechanism:
Session selection follows a fixed precedence after conflicting options are rejected. Naming and missing-directory recovery happen before model validation, so they can have visible effects even when later startup fails.

A truthy --fork conflicts with truthy session/continue/resume/noSession, but may combine with --session-id. A defined sessionId conflicts with truthy session/continue/resume and is always passed through assertValidSessionId; it may combine with no-session. These checks run after metadata/export short-circuits and before migrations. Directory precedence is truthy CLI session-dir normalized as a path, then truthy ENV_SESSION_DIR with tilde expansion, then startup settings sessionDir (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:255-292; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:620-627; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:648-652).

Selection branch order is noSession/help/listModels→inMemory, fork, session, resume, continue, sessionId lookup, then create. In-memory creation receives a defined requested ID. Fork first checks an exact local target-ID collision when a target ID is truthy, resolves its source and creates a fork with requested cwd/sessionDir/id. A session argument containing slash, backslash or ending '.jsonl' is resolved as a direct path; other values search local exact ID, local first prefix, global exact ID, global first prefix. There is no ambiguity rejection. Direct/local session matches open; a global ID match prints its source cwd and asks whether to fork into launch cwd. Only case-insensitive exact y/yes accepts, without trimming. That readline confirmation has no app-mode guard. Declining exits 0. This is a source-visible protocol risk if invoked through a noninteractive startup route, not a claim that such an invocation was executed (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:213-253; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:314-369).

Resume supplies both local and all-project asynchronous loaders to the startup picker, exits 0 on no selection, and stops the theme watcher in finally. Continue delegates to continueRecent; its absence fallback creates a new session under SESSION-032. A remaining requested ID opens an exact local match or warns and creates a new session with that ID. Open/fork errors are caught, printed and exit 1 (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:294-312; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:371-405).

After selection, a missing stored cwd prompts Continue with the current cwd or Cancel only in interactive mode; acceptance reopens the session with the fallback cwd, cancellation exits 0, and noninteractive modes fail with MissingSessionCwdError and code 1. A defined --name is trimmed and must be nonempty; it appends session_info before any model validation. Tests explicitly expect the name to persist even when a later missing-model error exits 1, and no append for whitespace-only name (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:654-674; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/startup-session-name.test.ts:110-135).
entries.interfaces: Selection accepts --no-session, --fork <path|id>, --session <path|id>, --resume/-r, --continue/-c, --session-id, --session-dir and --name/-n. Direct path resolution is distinct from ID discovery. Empty versus undefined option values matter. SESSION-029/031 own valid-ID and creation/persistence rules; CLI owns validation timing and branch precedence.
entries.dependency_text: Session storage, rich discovery, fork branch projection and identity validation remain SESSION contracts. TUI session picker behavior is reached through CLI-016.
entries.rust:
Native select_session prioritizes no_session, then continue/resume, fork, session_id, session. It applies no TS conflict validation and defaults its root to cwd/.ice/sessions, with only flag then saved setting overriding it. app resolves --resume into a picker result before provider/harness creation and requires both TTYs; the picker uses the default project directory rather than the supplied session-dir. --continue has an error when no resumable metadata exists instead of the TS fresh-session fallback (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/session.rs:154-192; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:617-638; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/resume_picker.rs:16-26; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/session.rs:2096-2135).

Native ById searches the selected directory using one first-match predicate (exact ID OR path contains query OR query contains ID); it does not perform the TS direct-path/global exact-before-prefix algorithm. Fork searches only its default root, ignores selected session-dir and requested target ID, and creates with id=None. Native name is applied during build_prepared after provider resolution, whitespace clears the name, and failures are only warned when verbose. Missing-cwd restore always warns and continues using native startup cwd, without TS interactive approval or headless failure (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/session.rs:2498-2519; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/session.rs:2137-2184; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/session.rs:400-422; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/session.rs:2676-2713).
entries.port: Implement one explicit validated startup selection plan before runtime creation. Preserve exact-ID collision checks, path-versus-ID resolution, custom directory handling and requested-name timing. Add cwd recovery with a typed noninteractive error and interactive decision. Keep the native TTY check for resume as a useful safeguard; avoid copying the unguarded cross-project readline prompt into RPC/JSON execution. Resolve global-session behavior through a mode-aware decision channel. Retain native storage formats under SESSION's migration plan rather than treating a path match as format compatibility.
entries.priority_reason: Incorrect session precedence or cwd selection can append to the wrong conversation or execute in an unintended project; naming timing is independently tested.

entries.title: CLI model, thinking, fast-mode and tool-option precedence
entries.what: Parsed model and tool flags are converted into a session configuration without erasing saved or restored choices unnecessarily. Scoped models and thinking suffixes have their own fallback precedence, and a CLI API key is a runtime-only override.
entries.mechanism:
CLI model choices override saved or scoped defaults only under specific conditions. The resulting options preserve the distinction between an omitted setting, an explicit false value and an empty list.

buildSessionOptions resolves a CLI model only when parsed.model is truthy, passing provider/model/thinking together. It preserves warning/error diagnostics and installs a resolved model when present. A resolved ':thinking' suffix applies only without an explicit parsed.thinking and sets cliThinkingFromModel. A provider-only flag does not itself assign options.model in this helper (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:407-447).

If no model was selected, scopedModels is nonempty and the existing session context has no messages, choose the saved provider/model when that exact model is in scope, otherwise the first scoped model. Its explicit scoped thinking applies only without CLI thinking. A truthy explicit thinking value then overrides both suffix and scope. A defined fastMode, including false, is copied. Nonempty scoped models are copied as {model,thinkingLevel}, retaining undefined thinking to mean inherit during cycling. This helper does not apply a scope fallback to an existing conversation and does not silently discard earlier model-resolution errors (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:449-487; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:780-787).

Tool precedence is noTools→'all', else noBuiltinTools→'builtin'; parsed tools and excludeTools arrays are copied even when empty arrays. The downstream registry decides active tool semantics. CLI model patterns override settings enabledModels by nullish choice, so an explicit empty array is distinct from absence. A truthy --api-key is installed through modelRuntime.setRuntimeApiKey only when session options already contain a model; otherwise a diagnostic requires --model or --models. No credential is persisted by this step. After session creation, explicit CLI thinking or a model suffix triggers setThinkingLevel on the created session's actual level, ensuring its durable change is recorded (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:489-505; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:770-831).
entries.interfaces: buildSessionOptions returns {options,cliThinkingFromModel,diagnostics}; options include model,thinkingLevel,fastMode,scopedModels,noTools,tools,excludeTools. Model matching and scope syntax belong to AUTH-024/025, shared thinking support/clamp to AI-005 and session changes to SESSION-036.
entries.dependency_text: AUTH-005 owns runtime credential override semantics; SET-011 owns default/scoped/queue persistence. SESSION-023 applies the tool registry policy and SESSION-036 owns resulting model/thinking state transitions.
entries.rust: Native app resolves the model/provider before restoring/building the session. Its --models branch compares each supplied value to catalog model IDs using ASCII case-insensitive equality, reports unmatched values, preserves repeated matches, and writes the result directly into global settings.scoped_models; zero matches become None. It is neither TS pattern resolution nor transient session scope construction (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:255-302). Native tool construction and merged active-name filtering are real and must be reused (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/session.rs:379-398; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/session.rs:2060-2068). Native parser lacks fast/no-fast and ultra as builtin options; AUTH-025/026 and AI-005 record broader model/restore/clamp differences instead of duplicating them here.
entries.port: Move native CLI option application behind the same resolved-session/service stage as its SDK, preserving existing native tool filtering. Implement scoped pattern matching through AUTH-024, keep CLI scope transient unless the product explicitly chooses persistence, apply saved-in-scope fallback only for an empty conversation, and persist the actual explicit thinking change through SESSION-036. Install API-key overrides only in memory and preserve false/empty-array distinctions.
entries.priority_reason: Model/scope precedence changes the provider used for a prompt and currently mutates saved native scope unexpectedly compared with TS.

entries.title: Piped stdin ownership, complete-input collection and read failures
entries.what: A piped prompt is consumed only when the application owns stdin, and is accepted only after a complete successful read. Read failures must not turn into an apparently valid prompt that omits the user's piped input.
entries.mechanism:
A pipe is accepted as prompt content only after a complete read. The application leaves stdin untouched when a terminal or protocol endpoint owns it and reports read failures instead of silently omitting input.

readPipedStdin first returns undefined for isTTY, then throws a preexisting input.errored, then returns undefined for readableEnded or destroyed. Consequently a TTY takes precedence over an error and an already destroyed nonerrored stream is treated as exhausted. For the real process.stdin under Bun with Bun.stdin, it awaits Bun.stdin.text, trims the outer whitespace and returns undefined for an empty result (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/piped-stdin.ts:1-21).

The Node stream path installs data/end/error/close listeners, uses setEncoding('utf8') and resume, accumulates the full text without a size limit, and resolves only on end after trim. A settled guard makes completion idempotent. Cleanup removes all listeners. Error rejects with the actual error. Close succeeds only if readableEnded is already true; otherwise it rejects input.errored or a specific premature-EOF error. There is no deadline or streaming prompt delivery. The tests cover split multibyte UTF-8, internal whitespace, empty/exhausted input, no TTY consumption, premature close and propagated failures (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/piped-stdin.ts:23-55; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/piped-stdin.test.ts:6-53).

Main invokes it only outside RPC, after the runtime has been built. A returned nonempty value can downgrade interactive mode to print and drain captured extension console output. RPC stdin remains the JSONL command channel (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:861-870).
entries.interfaces: readPipedStdin(input:Readable & {isTTY?:boolean}=process.stdin)→Promise<string|undefined>. Undefined means no usable piped content; rejection means the input was not read completely. Outer whitespace is removed; internal whitespace is preserved. No default byte cap or timeout is imposed at this helper.
entries.dependency_text: CLI-010 combines the completed text with attachments and the first CLI message. CLI-019 owns output-stream routing; RPC-016 owns stdin when command mode is selected.
entries.rust: Native app deliberately waits until extensions are loaded to determine owns_stdio and validates the stdio lifecycle before reading. It skips reads for rpc/server or a plugin stdio claim, a native capability that should be retained (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:221-235; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:315-342). Its reader has an ICE_SKIP_STDIN='1' escape hatch, skips TTYs, calls blocking read_to_string and trims successful input, but maps every read/UTF-8 error to None. Thus it can proceed with remaining CLI/file input after silently losing a failed pipe. It also performs the blocking read directly in the async startup path (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:770-800).
entries.port: Return a typed Result<Option<String>> from native stdin collection and fail startup when input is incomplete or unreadable. Retain stdio-claim/RPC ownership checks and exact outer trimming. Move blocking collection to an appropriate blocking task if the startup runtime must remain responsive. Define any future byte/time bound separately rather than claiming one exists in TS. Preserve the native test escape hatch only as an explicit documented extension.
entries.priority_reason: Silently dropping a failed piped prompt can execute an unintended partial request; complete-input semantics are directly covered by TS test source.

entries.title: CLI file attachments, typed text failures and image preprocessing
entries.what: File arguments become ordered text references and image attachments with safe preprocessing. The native CLI already attaches supported images; the remaining differences are path normalization, text validation and image transformation/error behavior.
entries.mechanism:
File arguments are processed in order into text references and image attachments. Image conversion and resizing run before delivery, while text failures carry a path and a typed reason.

processFileArguments accepts autoResizeImages default true, cwd default process.cwd and optional maxTextBytes default unlimited. It processes fileArgs sequentially. Each path passes resolveReadPath then resolve(cwd,...), which supplies tilde and platform filename normalization through the path helper. stat failure is reported as FileArgumentError('not_found'); nonregular files become 'unreadable'; zero-byte files are skipped entirely. It detects supported image MIME from file contents before choosing the branch (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/file-processor.ts:17-59).

Images are read and passed to processImage with the resolved MIME and auto-resize setting. A failed processing result adds a '<file name="absolutePath">message</file>\n' text reference and no image. Success appends an ImageContent carrying processed mime/data and a text reference containing joined processing hints or empty content. Conversion/resize logic belongs to TOOLS-023; the CLI always invokes it and does not consult blockImages here. The blockImages filter belongs to the later model conversion layer. Text files enforce maxTextBytes only when supplied, then read UTF-8 and wrap content in '<file name="absolutePath">\ncontent\n</file>\n'. Node decoding does not reject all invalid byte sequences like strict String::from_utf8. A text read exception becomes 'unreadable' with path and reason; image detection/read/processing exceptions are not wrapped by this text catch. Filename/content strings are not XML-escaped (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/file-processor.ts:61-99).

Main bypasses the helper for no file arguments. Otherwise it passes the session settings auto-resize flag, converts FileArgumentError into a printed error and process exit 1, and lets other exceptions propagate. The standalone CLI supplies neither a maxTextBytes limit nor a cwd option, so attachment relative paths use process cwd, distinct from launch-relative resource paths and potentially restored session cwd. RPC attachment handling supplies its own bounded options under RPC ownership. Existing tests assert BMP→PNG conversion hints, images even when later filtering is available, normal text, and omission when safe resize fails; none were executed here (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:163-195; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/block-images.test.ts:102-147; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/image-resize-callers.test.ts:44-52).
entries.interfaces: processFileArguments(string[],{autoResizeImages?,cwd?,maxTextBytes?})→Promise<{text,images}>. FileArgumentError codes: not_found,too_large,unreadable. Text references and images preserve argument order within their respective arrays/concatenation; empty files produce neither. Image processing is enabled by default.
entries.dependency_text: RPC-021 owns its attachment request boundary and size limits. TOOLS-020 owns shared read-path normalization, TOOLS-022 the ReadTool caller and TOOLS-023 image MIME/conversion/resize mechanics. SESSION-019 owns model-input preflight and later image policy. MISC-003 distinguishes later native user-image normalization from the CLI ingestion boundary and owns tool-result image normalization.
entries.rust: The native process_file_args resolves relative paths against startup cwd, checks existence, reads bytes, recognizes supported image MIME and base64-encodes images into the returned vector. Those images are passed into print/json/interactive mode calls. The app.rs header's claim that images are not wired is therefore contradicted by implementation and in-file image tests (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:238-244; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:393-423; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:807-856; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:988-1013). Native image attachments have no associated text reference, conversion/resize/hints or settings-driven autoResize step at this boundary. Empty text files produce an empty file wrapper, non-image invalid UTF-8 errors, and no typed maxTextBytes/regular-file contract exists here. Its errors return usage code 2. Later native user-message preprocessing calls normalize_user_images, which runs normalize_image_blocks on a blocking worker before prompt/queue admission; thus the missing CLI text references and settings option at ingestion do not establish globally absent native resizing (rust:crates/ice-harness/src/agent_harness.rs:4478-4495). MISC-003 records that later transport boundary and TOOLS-023 its algorithm.
entries.port: Retain native image attachment delivery and add the shared image preprocessing pipeline plus text reference/hints. Normalize paths through the shared tools path contract, skip zero-byte files, validate regular files and expose typed read/size errors. Decide strict versus replacement UTF-8 handling explicitly and document it. Keep CLI's currently unbounded text limit distinct from RPC's finite request contract. Do not mark image support missing because of stale comments.
entries.priority_reason: Attachment preprocessing controls usable image dimensions, format support and prompt provenance; native raw-image support is present but incomplete.

entries.title: Initial prompt concatenation and remaining-message ownership
entries.what: The initial prompt combines completed stdin, attachment text and the first positional message in that exact order. Remaining positional messages are retained for later turns rather than merged into one request.
entries.mechanism:
The initial prompt concatenates stdin, attachment text and one positional message without adding separators. Remaining messages stay available for later turns, and images travel separately.

buildInitialMessage pushes stdinContent whenever it is not undefined, including an empty string; pushes fileText only when truthy; and removes the first element from parsed.messages with shift whenever that array is nonempty, including an empty first message. It joins the pieces with an empty separator, so callers must supply any desired newlines. If no pieces exist the initialMessage is undefined, otherwise it can be the empty string. initialImages is the supplied nonempty image array itself or undefined; there is no clone or image-to-text merge. The function mutates parsed.messages and returns only {initialMessage,initialImages} (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/initial-message.ts:18-43).

The CLI passes attachment results and completed stdin into this helper, then hands the mutated remaining parsed.messages to interactive or print mode. Tests assert stdin+first-message combination and retention of a second message, with exact newline behavior supplied by fixture strings (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:163-180; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:953-991; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/initial-message.test.ts:14-48).
entries.interfaces: buildInitialMessage({parsed,stdinContent?,fileText?,fileImages?})→{initialMessage?:string,initialImages?:ImageContent[]}. No implicit separator, no trimming at this stage, and no deduplication. Whitespace normalization is performed earlier only by the stdin reader.
entries.dependency_text: The stdin and attachment owners produce the pieces. Session prompt execution decides how initial images and subsequent messages are delivered; the helper only assembles and transfers ownership.
entries.rust: Native build_initial_message clones parsed.messages, removes its first element from the clone, joins optional stdin/file text/first message with no separator and returns (Option<String>,Vec<String>). App converts empty aggregate file text to None before calling it. Images are passed separately into mode execution, so immutable Args plus an explicit remaining vector is a sound native representation of the live CLI contract. Direct helper calls with Some("") file text differ from TS's truthy fileText check, but the native app normalizes that case before use. Inline tests cover ordering, no messages, no inputs and one-message shifting (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:344-350; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:858-886; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:952-986).
entries.port: Keep the native clone-and-return representation and exact concatenation/order. Document direct helper empty-file-text normalization if exposing it as a public API, and preserve empty first messages plus separate image ownership. No replacement implementation is needed for the live startup concatenation itself; downstream attachment and session delivery differences are owned elsewhere.
entries.priority_reason: The live native assembly already matches the meaningful startup behavior; only helper representation/empty-option edges differ.

entries.title: Credential-print command grammar, output discipline and duration parsing defect
entries.what: Credential-print commands resolve a configured credential for external scripts and write only the value to stdout. They use an early, restricted command path so normal session startup output does not contaminate the result.
entries.mechanism:
Credential printing is handled before ordinary startup migrations and session creation. It has its own help, validation and error boundary, while sharing the normal model/auth resolver for the actual credential.

isCredentialPrintHelp accepts argv[0]='auth' with an absent second token or exact help/--help/-h, regardless of trailing tokens. Otherwise parseCredentialPrintCommand recognizes only print-api-key→api_key and print-bearer-token→bearer_token; any other auth subcommand throws CredentialPrintError. The parser removes exact '--min-expiry' plus its next token from the normal args, permits it only for bearer mode, and uses the last repeated value. Other spellings such as '--min-expiry=30m' pass through to normal parsing and are subsequently rejected as unknown flags (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/credential-print.ts:18-64).

The duration regexp accepts decimal digits followed by ms/s/m/h with case-insensitive matching, but the multiplier compares the captured unit case-sensitively. Thus '30S' or '30M' is accepted and multiplied as hours; 'MS' similarly falls into the hours branch. This is a concrete source defect, not intended minimum-expiry behavior. Zero is accepted and no safe-integer/finite cap exists, so extremely large numeric text can produce an infinite value. No whitespace, sign or decimal fractions are accepted. Default bearer minimum expiry is 30 minutes (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/credential-print.ts:8-13; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/credential-print.ts:43-63).

Validation requires a nonblank model, forbids any defined apiKey and rejects positional messages, file arguments and nonempty unknownFlags. It does not reject every other recognized normal flag despite the message saying only provider/model are accepted. Main treats any parse diagnostic, including a warning, as failure. It creates ModelRuntime with allowModelNetwork=false and one AbortSignal.timeout(15000) shared through runtime creation and credential resolution, writes the returned credential plus '\n' directly to stdout, and returns true. CredentialPrintError messages are printed to stderr; other errors use a generic message to avoid leaking resolver details. Failure sets process.exitCode=1 rather than immediately exiting (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/credential-print.ts:66-76; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:117-160).
entries.interfaces: 'ice auth print-api-key --model <model> [--provider <provider>]' and 'ice auth print-bearer-token ... [--min-expiry <duration>]'. Success: raw credential plus one LF, no JSON/banner. Failure: stderr plus exitCode 1. Model-network catalog discovery is disabled, but OAuth request-auth refresh can still occur through CLI-012.
entries.dependency_text: CLI-012 owns candidate-provider inference and request-auth extraction. AUTH-004 owns refresh/credential persistence; disabling model discovery is not a blanket network prohibition on an explicitly requested credential refresh.
entries.rust: Native auth dispatch supports login, check/status, refresh, logout and help. Other subcommands, including these two print names, produce an unknown-command error and code 2. Native check JSON reports readiness/source; it is not a credential-value endpoint (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/auth.rs:35-65; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/auth.rs:115-150). The required early output discipline, duration option and one credential-result boundary are missing.
entries.port: Add the two explicit print routes before session/runtime output, using the shared native credential resolver and a bounded cancellation/deadline context. Normalize the duration unit before multiplying and reject nonfinite/overflowing durations; decide whether zero is supported. Replace TS's misleading partial argument whitelist with an explicit accepted set, documenting any compatibility change. Preserve credential-only stdout and generic handling of unexpected resolver failures. Do not copy the uppercase-unit defect.
entries.priority_reason: Scripts need a deterministic credential-only command; parser errors and incidental startup output can otherwise break integrations or expose diagnostics.

entries.title: Credential-print provider inference, refresh policy and ambiguity handling
entries.what: Credential printing chooses one provider/model request credential, using configured credential metadata to avoid guessing among unrelated providers. It rejects ambiguous usable matches and refreshes OAuth through the same request-auth path used for model calls.
entries.mechanism:
The resolver first validates the CLI arguments and lists credential metadata. It uses that metadata to select eligible providers, then resolves and extracts a single usable value without exposing candidate credentials in an ambiguity error.

A Map of providerId→credential type is built from modelRuntime.listCredentials({signal}). With a truthy explicit provider, resolveCliModel receives the requested provider/model and any error or absent model becomes CredentialPrintError. Without a provider, iterate getProviders in registry order, skip providers absent from the credential metadata map, and resolve the model independently under each provider. Accept a model only without an error and without a warning containing the exact substring 'Using custom model id'. No accepted model is an explicit not-found error. Explicit provider resolution can admit a custom model; inferred candidates deliberately do not (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/credential-print.ts:91-114).

Candidates are processed sequentially. api_key mode skips a provider whose credential type is oauth but allows another or absent type; bearer mode requires type oauth. Each eligible model calls getAuth with the shared signal and, only for bearer mode, minOAuthValidityMs equal to the supplied duration or 1,800,000. The comment about a fixed five-minute refresh does not describe this caller's requested validity. It finds the first header whose name lowercases to authorization, parses a case-insensitive 'Bearer' followed by whitespace and nonempty content, and chooses auth.apiKey ?? parsedBearer for bearer mode or only auth.apiKey for key mode. An empty apiKey suppresses header fallback through nullish selection, then is rejected by the truthy-value check. Values are not additionally trimmed (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/credential-print.ts:116-132).

Exactly one usable value succeeds. Zero values yields a tailored wrong-credential-type error when an explicit provider was supplied, otherwise a generic no-usable-credential error. More than one usable candidate is ambiguous even when their credential strings happen to be equal; the error lists provider IDs only. Resolver/getAuth exceptions are not swallowed per candidate and abort the entire operation through main's generic error boundary. Tests exercise API keys, Authorization-header bearer extraction, expired-token refresh/persistence and explicit type rejection; source inspection does not imply the tests ran (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/credential-print.ts:134-151; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/credential-print.test.ts:22-103).
entries.interfaces: resolveCredentialForPrint(args,modelRuntime,'api_key'|'bearer_token',minExpiryMs?,signal?)→Promise<string>. Uses listCredentials/getProviders/resolveCliModel/getAuth. Does not return a list of secrets, select the first ambiguous candidate, or persist the CLI apiKey flag.
entries.dependency_text: AUTH-003 provides credential metadata enumeration, AUTH-004 request-auth refresh and storage preservation, AUTH-024/025 model reference/matching semantics. CLI owns only the single-value resolution policy.
entries.rust: Native auth commands can inspect readiness, perform provider-owned OAuth refresh and store credentials, but the dispatch has no print-value command or this model-based candidate inference. A native provider credential source is not sufficient without the explicit type filtering, minimum-validity request, header fallback and ambiguity contract (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/auth.rs:44-65; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/auth.rs:115-150). Provider-specific OAuth implementations remain separately verified/unverified under AUTH; this entry does not assume concrete flows exist merely because generic host hooks do.
entries.port: Implement candidate inference using the native provider catalog and credential metadata, then call AUTH's resolver rather than reading auth.json directly. Preserve type filtering, requested validity, cancellation and ambiguity. Use a structured custom-model indicator instead of depending on a human warning substring when designing the native API, while matching observed TS selection behavior. Retain stored credentials on transient refresh failure according to AUTH-004.
entries.priority_reason: Returning a credential from the wrong provider or skipping refresh breaks consumers; the inference and failure rules are more specific than ordinary auth readiness checks.

entries.title: Credential startup migration and recoverable native layout migration
entries.what: Startup migrations convert old credential storage into the current location without changing current literal configuration values. Both implementations contain failure-order problems that must be repaired when carrying migration support forward.
entries.mechanism:
The TS conversion is skipped entirely when auth.json already exists. Otherwise it gathers old OAuth entries and settings API keys into one object, then writes the new credential file after changing the old sources.

For oauth.json, parse JSON and iterate Object.entries without validating each credential shape; assign {type:'oauth',...cred}, so a supplied cred.type can override the inserted discriminator, append provider names and rename the old file to oauth.json.migrated. All errors in that block are swallowed, including a failed rename after values were already gathered. For settings.json, parse it and inspect truthy object-valued apiKeys; arrays are not explicitly rejected. Add only string values whose provider currently has no truthy entry, so gathered OAuth entries take precedence. Delete settings.apiKeys and rewrite settings with two-space JSON. This block also swallows errors. If the gathered object is nonempty, mkdir and write auth.json with mode 0600 occur outside both catches; an error propagates and prevents later migrations (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts:20-72).

The order is not transactional: a successfully rewritten settings file may no longer contain its API keys when final auth.json creation fails, and oauth.json may already have been renamed. This is a source-derived data-loss/recovery risk, not a reproduced runtime incident. Existing tests intentionally leave current uppercase API-key/header strings unchanged, leave malformed/blank models.json for its normal parser, and require no automatic conversion of bare uppercase literals into environment references. They do not validate final-write-failure rollback (ice:packages/coding-agent/test/config-value-migration.test.ts:41-177; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/suite/regressions/5661-uppercase-header-values.test.ts:33-90).
entries.interfaces: migrateAuthToAuthJson()→string[] migrated provider names. Inputs are only current agentDir oauth.json/settings.json, output auth.json, and OAuth backup suffix '.migrated'. runMigrations invokes this before session/tools/keybindings/resource migration. Actual user credential files were not read during this audit.
entries.dependency_text: AUTH owns credential schema/current store writes; SET owns literal/environment/command config resolution. Migration must not reinterpret bare uppercase strings or infer that old namespaces are aliases.
entries.rust: Rust migrates a different layout: default flat config-root auth.json/models.json/.setup_done into agent/. It skips whenever CONFIG_DIR_ENV is set, even empty, and when agent already exists. It only begins when flat auth or models exists, creates agent, attempts rename then copy/remove for each file, and increments moved even if both rename and copy fail. Since a created agent directory causes the next call to return 0, partial transfers do not resume despite the comment. app discards the Result; read_auth/load_models_config pass None as the fallback path, so stranded flat files are not read through that helper. This concrete failure/count defect is distinct from TS's credential-format conversion (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:176-225; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:187-191; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:260-269; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:408-416). Inline tests cover successful moves and existing-directory/no-input/env gates, not failed transfer recovery (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:1565-1611).
entries.port: Implement credential-format conversion as a staged, validated transaction: prepare and atomically publish the new auth store before retiring old sources, keep recoverable backups, and report failed finalization. For native flat-layout migration, decide per-file completion rather than agent-directory existence, increment counts only after verified transfer, and retain explicit failures for retry. Preserve existing destination data and override boundaries. Do not copy either implementation's failure-order defect or read real home state as part of this audit.
entries.priority_reason: Migration failure can strand credentials or remove their last normal lookup location; startup must remain recoverable without silently claiming success.

entries.title: Session, managed-binary, prompt-directory and keybinding startup migrations
entries.what: The startup migration sequence repairs several old layouts and reports deprecated extension directories. Each step has a separate scope and failure policy, and some project filesystem changes occur before the normal trust decision.
entries.mechanism:
runMigrations calls credential migration, flat-session migration, managed-binary relocation, keybinding-file migration and extension-system migration in that exact order. Its result is migratedAuthProviders plus deprecationWarnings; main later displays warnings only in interactive mode.

Session migration scans only *.jsonl directly in getAgentDir. It reads each entire file to inspect the first line, skips blank/invalid/non-session/missing-cwd headers, computes '--'+cwd with one leading slash/backslash removed and remaining slash/backslash/colon replaced by '-'+ '--', creates agentDir/sessions/encoded-cwd, skips an existing target and renames. Directory scan failure returns; each file's errors are swallowed. The filename expression file.split('/').pop() || file.split('\\').pop() is incorrect for an ordinary Windows backslash path: the first split already returns the entire truthy path, so the fallback never supplies a basename. This is a source-only platform defect; use a path basename operation in a port (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts:83-130).

Managed binaries are exactly fd,rg,fd.exe,rg.exe in agentDir/tools. Create getBinDir if needed, move a missing destination, or remove the old copy when the destination exists. Move/remove errors are ignored, but mkdir is outside their catch and can abort the sequence. A success message appears only after at least one rename; tools/ itself is not removed. Keybinding migration parses only a nonnull nonarray object, calls migrateKeybindingsConfig, writes two-space JSON plus LF only when changed, and swallows read/parse/write errors. TUI-048 owns the exact historical key translation (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts:156-215).

Extension migration attempts global commands→prompts, then project commands→prompts, only when source exists and target does not; directories or symlinks are renamed, and failures are printed as warnings. It then collects global and project warnings for hooks/ and for tools/ entries other than case-insensitive fd/rg/exe names and dot-prefixed names. The main call at line 628 precedes project trust resolution around lines 677 onward, so the project directory rename is not gated by the later project trust decision. The deprecation display prints warnings/guide URLs, enables raw input when supported, waits for one data event, disables raw mode and pauses stdin; it has no error/EOF listener (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts:136-154; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts:221-314; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:628-641; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:677-705; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:872-875).
entries.interfaces: runMigrations(cwd)→{migratedAuthProviders:string[],deprecationWarnings:string[]}. Inputs include global agentDir and project configuration directory for the supplied launch cwd. Targets are sessions/<encoded-cwd>, bin, prompts and keybindings.json. showDeprecationWarnings returns immediately for an empty list; otherwise awaits a keypress.
entries.dependency_text: SESSION owns actual session format migration/discovery, TUI-048 pure keybinding renames, SET-003 trust decisions. This entry owns on-disk invocation, ordering, boundaries and failures; managed-tool installation is a separate MISC dependency.
entries.rust: The inspected native startup invokes only config::migrate_legacy_layout at this stage, which moves three flat credential/model/setup files. It does not implement these TS session-placement, fd/rg relocation, commands/prompts or keybinding-file transformations. Native session storage has its own format/version and current project-root layout, so renaming a TS file alone would not make it loadable (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:187-203; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:169-225; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/session.rs:154-192). Existing native configuration and package discovery are retained rather than replaced by these legacy helpers.
entries.port: Implement each needed migration as a separately recorded, repeatable operation with explicit source/destination validation and error reporting. Use platform basename logic, keep existing targets intact, and connect session format conversion to SESSION-029 rather than blindly relocating incompatible logs. Gate project mutations at the intended trust stage instead of inheriting an implicit pre-trust rename. Give interactive warning acknowledgement an EOF/error/cancellation exit so it cannot wait forever on a closed terminal.
entries.priority_reason: Legacy users need predictable migration, but the current functions contain swallowed failures and a Windows path defect that should not be preserved.

entries.title: Official first-run gate and startup theme bootstrap
entries.what: The TS first-run dialog is a narrowly gated onboarding flow that selects a theme and analytics preference. Startup selectors share a smaller theme loader that avoids relying on project resources before trust is resolved.
entries.mechanism:
First-run setup is shown only for the official experimental distribution with no existing settings file. Startup theme preparation uses global settings and installed enabled themes, then adapts to the terminal's background without blocking normal startup on a broken theme.

Official identity requires the exact triple @zykairotis/ice-coding-agent, ice and .ice. shouldRunFirstTimeSetup returns false for any other triple, when experimental features are disabled, or when process.env[ENV_AGENT_DIR] is truthy; an empty override does not suppress it. Otherwise it returns !existsSync(settingsPath). Main additionally requires interactive mode and neither help nor list-models, and invokes it after migrations but before session selection (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/startup-ui.ts:26-42; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/startup-ui.ts:108-132; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:632-641).

loadStartupThemes constructs in-memory settings from the global snapshot with projectTrusted=false, creates a package manager at process cwd/agent dir and resolves missing packages with an async 'skip' answer. Only enabled theme resources are loaded. A duplicate truthy theme name is first-wins; unnamed themes are not deduplicated. Theme load errors are ignored for later normal diagnostics. createStartupTui registers these themes, selects the environment-detected background and resolved setting, installs global keybindings, and creates a TuiMainScreen with hardware-cursor and clear-on-shrink settings. startStartupTui starts the terminal then fires an unawaited detection update only for absent/auto theme settings; detection is capped at 100 ms, then setTheme/invalidate/requestRender run without a disposal-generation check (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/startup-ui.ts:44-100).

The first-time dialog starts UI, awaits its own 100-ms terminal theme detection, sets that theme and installs preview/submit/cancel callbacks. A settled guard is set before asynchronous finalization. Submit sets theme and shareAnalytics, awaits settings.flush, clears/render-waits 25 ms, stops UI and resolves. Cancel omits persistence but follows clear/stop. Normal SettingsManager.flush awaits a queue whose write errors are caught and recorded, so ordinary persistence failure can be recorded while the dialog proceeds (SET-009). There is no outer rejection/finally around finalization: an unexpected rejected finalizer or terminal operation is not propagated by the void callbacks and can leave the resolve-only startup Promise unsettled. This narrower source-derived cleanup risk is not an executed failure (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/startup-ui.ts:102-106; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/startup-ui.ts:165-205).
entries.interfaces: shouldRunFirstTimeSetup(settingsPath=getSettingsPath())→boolean; createStartupTui(settings)→Promise<TUI>; startStartupTui(ui,settings)→void; showFirstTimeSetup(settings)→Promise<void>. Persistence uses the normal settings manager. TUI-070 owns the dialog's visual fields and input behavior; this entry owns its startup gate and lifetime.
entries.dependency_text: SET-017 owns theme preferences and SET-018 analytics consent/tracking persistence. The package supplement owns startup theme resource resolution, and TUI-070 owns questionnaire presentation. This entry owns the caller gate and terminal lifetime.
entries.rust: Native extras uses an agentDir/.setup_done sentinel. Whenever absent, maybe_first_time_setup adds a static welcome/theme/help banner, best-effort writes '1' and returns true. It honors a custom native config-dir path and does not check official distribution, experimental features or settings-file existence. The interactive caller captures existing-profile status, calls this banner and then handles changelog presentation; no theme/analytics questionnaire is wired there. Native in-file tests cover sentinel placement under an override (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/extras.rs:11-64; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/extras.rs:75-93; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/interactive_tui.rs:1009-1028). This is a real first-launch banner with a different gate, not equivalent TS onboarding.
entries.port: Choose and document the native first-run product policy, then implement the required official/experimental/settings gate if TS compatibility is intended. Reuse native theme/input components for TUI-070 and persist selections through SET. Make asynchronous finalization reject or settle exactly once with guaranteed terminal cleanup, and prevent delayed theme detection from rendering after disposal. Keep the existing banner as a distinct optional native feature rather than counting it as completed onboarding.
entries.priority_reason: Onboarding is conditional rather than a universal startup gap, but terminal lifetime and preference persistence need precise behavior.

entries.title: Startup selectors, config wrapper and resume-picker terminal lifetime
entries.what: Short-lived startup dialogs own the terminal until they choose, cancel or quit, then return control to startup. The wrappers pass settings, scope and asynchronous data loaders into richer TUI components rather than implementing those widgets themselves.
entries.mechanism:
Generic startup selector/input wrappers resolve once and stop their temporary TUI after clearing it. Config and session wrappers additionally define which child receives focus and which operation exits the whole process.

showStartupSelector creates the shared startup TUI, passes only option labels to ExtensionSelectorComponent and maps a selected label back with options.find, so duplicate labels choose the first matching value. Its finish marks settled before awaiting clearStartupTui's 25-ms render wait, then stops and resolves; cancellation resolves undefined. showStartupInput has the same guard/order but first disposes its input component, then clears/stops and resolves the string or undefined. Both start through startStartupTui, which may have an asynchronous theme-detection update in flight. There is no outer rejection/finally path around failed asynchronous completion (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/startup-ui.ts:134-163; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/startup-ui.ts:207-239).

selectConfig initializes the current theme with watching enabled, creates a TuiMainScreen with supplied agentDir, and passes resolved resource paths/settings/cwd/agentDir, terminal rows, writeScope ('global'|'project') and projectModeAvailable to ConfigSelectorComponent. Done is guarded, stops UI and theme watcher, then resolves. Quit stops both and process.exit(0). Render requests delegate to UI, and initial focus is the resource list (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/config-selector.ts:10-55).

selectSession awaits startup TUI, creates/installs keybindings and passes current/all-session loaders to SessionSelectorComponent. Selection resolves a session path, cancel resolves null and both stop UI once; quit stops UI and exits 0. It disables the rename hint and focuses the session list. The wrapper itself does not stop the theme watcher, but main's resume branch does so in finally. TUI-062/063/064 own search/list/loading/rename/delete details (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/session-picker.ts:12-55; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:371-385).
entries.interfaces: showStartupSelector<T>(settings,title,{label,value}[])→Promise<T|undefined>; showStartupInput(settings,title,placeholder?)→Promise<string|undefined>; selectConfig(options)→Promise<void>; selectSession(currentLoader,allLoader,settings)→Promise<string|null>. Scope availability and resource mutation remain the package/TUI component contracts.
entries.dependency_text: TUI owns widgets, keybindings and rich session operations. The package supplement owns 'ice config' routing and resource resolution, while this entry owns the callable wrapper and terminal cleanup. Generic extension selector/input components need their TUI entry links before publication.
entries.rust: Native resume_picker is implemented: it lists project metadata, computes bounded summaries on spawn_blocking, removes empty rows, creates a 12-row SelectList with 56–72-column primary layout, and starts TuiAltScreen with a render scheduler. A blocking crossterm loop polls every 100 ms, handles resize/mouse scroll, filters typed text, clears a nonempty query on Esc and cancels on empty-query Esc or Ctrl+C. It stops the TUI after the input task completes, including task errors. Empty metadata or no resumable rows is an error rather than an empty rich selector. It does not provide current/all loaders, the TS startup config resource wrapper or generic typed label-value/input wrappers (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/resume_picker.rs:16-188). Its tests cover age/label/byte/id formatting; source only (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/resume_picker.rs:190-246).
entries.port: Reuse the native temporary terminal and selector lifecycle, extending it through the TUI owners for all-project loading and config resources. Add generic typed selector/input adapters with stable value identity rather than label lookup when duplicate labels are allowed. Guarantee stop and callback settlement on every error/cancel path, coordinate delayed theme work with disposal, and preserve the explicit distinction between cancel-return and process quit.
entries.priority_reason: A native resume picker exists, but startup configuration and consistent temporary-terminal cleanup need additional integration.

entries.title: Available-model listing, fuzzy filtering and stable tabular output
entries.what: The TS list-models command reports models usable with current runtime credentials, then filters and sorts the result for display. The native command intentionally inspects a broader catalog before authenticated session creation, which is useful but not the same contract.
entries.mechanism:
Model listing warns about configuration load errors before querying availability. It then prints a six-column table or a clear empty-result message, with provider/model ordering independent of fuzzy-match score.

listModels first reads modelRuntime.getError and prints a yellow models.json warning when present. It awaits getAvailable(undefined,{signal}) and copies the result. A completely empty available set prints the shared no-models guidance and returns before filtering. A truthy search pattern uses fuzzyFilter over only 'provider id', not display name. Zero filtered matches prints the exact requested pattern. Remaining models sort by provider.localeCompare, then id.localeCompare, so fuzzy relevance does not control final row ordering (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/list-models.ts:29-62).

Rows contain provider, model ID, context window, max output, reasoning yes/no and image-input yes/no.
