Token counts use M at one million or above, K at one thousand or above, with no decimal for an exact integral multiple and one decimal otherwise. Column widths use the maximum header/string length, each cell is padEnd-aligned and columns join with two spaces. Main passes a 15-second signal and a string search only when listModels is a string, after runtime/extensions are created but before ordinary startup diagnostic failure handling (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/list-models.ts:14-24; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/cli/list-models.ts:64-115; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:847-858).
entries.interfaces: listModels(modelRuntime,searchPattern?,signal?)→Promise<void>; --list-models optionally consumes one nonflag/nonfile search token. Table headers are provider,model,context,max-out,thinking,images. Output uses no JSON schema. Availability and fuzzy matching are dependency contracts, not inferred from catalog membership.
entries.dependency_text: AUTH-006 owns availability with credential metadata, AUTH-024 model reference matching, AI-002 catalog/runtime lifecycle. The actual fuzzyFilter utility is low-level TUI-owned; this entry records its key and subsequent sorting.
entries.rust: Native list_models runs before provider credentials, session restoration and harness creation. It prepares extensions, obtains their manifests and loads the merged catalog. Config error warns and yields an empty catalog. Search trims and ASCII-lowercases a substring over provider,id,name; it does not call TS fuzzyFilter or available-model filtering. It retains catalog order without the explicit provider/ID locale sort. The six columns and K/M formatting are substantially equivalent, using native byte lengths for computed widths. Its broader unauthenticated catalog inspection is explicitly stated at the call site and should be preserved as a deliberate mode if desired (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:197-203; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:654-768).
entries.port: Provide a clear choice between available models and all catalog models, rather than silently equating the two. For TS-compatible --list-models, use AUTH availability, the agreed fuzzy matcher and deterministic provider/model sorting, with the same empty/error output and cancellation. Retain native unauthenticated catalog inspection under an explicit documented option or deliberate compatibility decision.
entries.priority_reason: Both list models, but filtering and availability semantics differ enough to mislead users about which model can actually run.

entries.title: Exact identity helpers, canonical paths and deliberately limited legacy compatibility
entries.what: The current compatibility helpers preserve exact current names and paths rather than broadly translating old Pi or PIV state. Historical module imports are supported through a small explicit alias table, which is separate from environment, settings and storage migration.
entries.mechanism:
Canonical configuration lookup does not search old product trees or reinterpret namespace names. The only broad-looking legacy helpers are shallow copies; actual module aliases are explicit data consumed by the extension loader.

getCompatibleConfigEnv checks an own property of the scoped map first when its value is not undefined, then the same exact own name in ambient environment, otherwise undefined. Empty strings are valid and override ambient values; scoped undefined falls back. getIceEnv reads only an own property of the supplied exact name. normalizeLegacyEnvironment shallow-copies all enumerable own fields and does not create ICE aliases. clearSessionEnvironment deletes exactly ICE_SESSION_ID,ICE_SESSION_FILE,ICE_PROVIDER,ICE_MODEL,ICE_REASONING_LEVEL (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/legacy-compat/env.ts:1-31).

matchesEntryType is strict equality. normalizeLegacySettings rejects null, arrays and nonobjects, then returns a shallow copy without converting a piv namespace. compatibleConfigRoot simply joins parent and configDirName (default '.ice'); it does not inspect existence, legacy .pi directories or dangling canonical symlinks. Cognee and Blackhole helpers return agentDir/ice-cognee and agentDir/ice-blackhole/ice-blackhole-config.json. Tests explicitly reject implicit PIV/PI environment promotion, historical journal-envelope equality and old-tree fallback while preserving exact-name scoped precedence (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/legacy-compat/identity.ts:1-10; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/legacy-compat/paths.ts:1-6; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/legacy-compat/cognee.ts:1-9; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/legacy-compat/identity-inputs.test.ts:5-34; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/legacy-compat/paths-and-cli.test.ts:17-40; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/legacy-compat/config-references.test.ts:11-46).

The alias table contains seven exact suffixes for each of @earendil-works and @mariozechner: pi-coding-agent→@zykairotis/ice-coding-agent, pi-agent-core→ice-agent-core, pi-tui→ice-tui, pi-ai→ice-ai, pi-ai/compat→ice-ai/compat, pi-ai/oauth→ice-ai/oauth, and pi-ai/providers/all→ice-ai/providers/all, with the @zykairotis scope on every target. The data module does no filesystem or loader work. EXT-002 owns runtime-specific resolution and unsupported-subpath rejection. The full built-runtime test source checks opt-in Node/Bun artifacts and exact aliases, but was not executed or treated as proof that built outputs are fresh (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/legacy-compat/extension-aliases.ts:17-36; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/legacy-compat/built-runtime-smoke.test.ts:10-24; ice:packages/coding-agent/test/legacy-compat/built-runtime-smoke.test.ts:62-212).
entries.interfaces: CompatibilityEnvironment is Readonly<Record<string,string|undefined>>. Helpers are exact-name operations with shallow-copy semantics. The one launcher PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR nullish bridge belongs to CLI-002, and current on-disk transformations belong to CLI-013/014. No general old-home-state import is implied.
entries.dependency_text: SET-001 owns current distribution paths, SET-005 config expression lookup and SET-010 actual settings migration. EXT-002 owns historical module aliases. Cognee/Blackhole storage users keep their existing area contracts.
entries.rust: Native agent_dir uses exactly ICE_CODING_AGENT_DIR when present and absolute, otherwise home/.ice/agent; its default session root is cwd/.ice/sessions. These are canonical native rules, with a separate default flat-layout migration rather than implicit .pi/PIV fallback (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:89-108; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/config.rs:176-225; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/session.rs:189-192). Rust typed settings/environment APIs do not need literal JS shallow-copy functions, but must preserve their exact-name contract at compatibility boundaries. Native package/extension interoperability is assessed by EXT-001/002 and the package supplement; no blanket 'Rust cannot load any Pi package' conclusion is drawn from these helper files.
entries.port: Preserve canonical-name and no-implicit-old-tree behavior in native configuration and migration APIs. Retain exact supported module aliases through the real bridge/loader owner, without wildcard prefix rewrites or guessed subpaths. Do not implement the first-pass claim of broad old environment/path mapping because the frozen TS code intentionally does not do it. Document any deliberate native path-layout difference under SET/SESSION rather than hiding it behind 'legacy compatibility'.
entries.priority_reason: The main audit correction is avoiding an invented migration feature; actual alias support and small identity boundaries remain important.

entries.title: Offline normalization, startup diagnostics, output ownership and shutdown integration
entries.what: Startup coordinates output ownership, optional recording/dashboard services and mode shutdown so protocol output remains usable. Offline and benchmark flags also change startup work before the selected mode begins.
entries.mechanism:
Offline mode is normalized before early command routing, and stream ownership is chosen before migrations or runtime creation can print. Mode execution later shares one recorder/dashboard lifetime with an explicit cleanup boundary.

Main checks raw args.includes('--offline') or envTruthy(ICE_OFFLINE) and, when enabled, assigns both ICE_OFFLINE='1' and ICE_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK='1'. This raw scan is independent of whether the normal parser would consume that token as another flag's value. On win32 it then invokes self-update quarantine cleanup, captures launch cwd and applies bootstrap global proxy settings. SET-013 owns proxy/dispatcher behavior; MISC-002 owns Windows native-dependency quarantine cleanup. reportDiagnostics sends errors, warnings and neutral diagnostics to stderr with red/yellow/dim coloring and matching prefixes; settings errors are drained into warning values annotated with startup/runtime and scope (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:73-94; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:530-552).

Noninteractive mode takes over stdout unless it is the exact plain-runtime-metadata predicate. Interactive nonmetadata startup enables extension console capture. After runtime creation, help/list can exit before normal runtime error reporting. For a later stdin-driven downgrade to print, captured console output is disabled/drained to stderr. Once input/theme setup is complete, interactive mode alone shows deprecation warnings; then runtime diagnostics print, any error exits 1, and an extension-load error adds the '-ne' hint. These are ordered caller actions; EXT-007 owns capture buffering and RPC-017/output guard owns the lower stream mechanism (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:615-627; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:847-887).

Nonoffline RPC starts a background modelRuntime.refresh with a 15-second AbortController timer, ignores failure and clears the timer in finally. Every ordinary agent run then attempts to open agentDir/observability.sqlite and start one recorder with Cognee observations; failure warns and continues. Optional --observe starts the dashboard with that recorder/replay store, agentDir/observe.token and cwd-bound Cognee source. Its URL is queued as an interactive notice or printed to stderr. Dashboard startup failure stops the recorder and rethrows before the mode try/finally. OBS-003/004/014/016 own the services themselves (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:896-946).

The mode try prints timings and invokes RPC, interactive or print with the initial/remaining messages. ICE_STARTUP_BENCHMARK uses the same truthy convention, errors outside interactive mode, initializes the TUI without running a conversation, waits 150 ms for terminal replies, stops UI/theme watching, prints timings and waits for stdout then stderr drain only when each writableLength is positive. Print-mode completion stops theme watching, restores stdout, sets a nonzero exitCode when returned, then returns. The final block closes an observeServer when present, otherwise stops the recorder. It is not a general runtime.dispose finally; individual modes own their own runtime/terminal cleanup (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:890-895; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/main.ts:948-1007).
entries.interfaces: Environment surfaces: ICE_OFFLINE,ICE_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK,ICE_STARTUP_BENCHMARK. --observe is true or a validated port; dashboard token/history paths are agentDir-relative. Startup errors and notices route to stderr unless explicitly buffered for TUI. No tests or benchmark were executed during the audit.
entries.dependency_text: OBS owns timing, recording, token/HTTP and shared-port behavior. SET-013 owns proxy/idle preferences and the HTTP dispatcher; MISC-001 owns version metadata/checks and MISC-002 Windows loaded native-dependency quarantine. RPC-020 owns JSONL shutdown/rebinding, not every CLI mode.
entries.rust: Native run wraps run_inner and prints timing after it returns. Native offline normalization sets ICE_OFFLINE but not the TS ICE_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK marker. It has its own --connect early route, static warnings only under verbose, plugin-owned stdio validation, ICE_SKIP_STDIN/ICE_FORCE_TUI controls, and cleanup of dev watcher/context/harness after mode execution. RPC/server dispatch contains real extension lifecycle and JSONL/plugin-stdio choices (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:73-103; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/args.rs:31-71; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:315-381; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:434-520; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/app.rs:640-650). The startup path lacks the TS recorder/dashboard, extension console buffering, benchmark and stdout takeover sequence; these are specific integrations rather than absence of all cleanup or timing.
entries.port: Integrate the existing native modes with explicit output ownership and one cleanup owner for each service. Reuse OBS's recorder/dashboard without duplicating subscriptions, preserve plugin stdio ownership, and make offline gating consistent across raw preflight and parsed commands. Implement the startup benchmark only as a bounded initialization path with guaranteed terminal restoration, rather than a hidden conversation run. Keep stream restoration and runtime disposal contracts visible at mode boundaries.
entries.priority_reason: Startup output contamination and mismatched cleanup can break RPC/scripts; several native lifecycle pieces already exist and should be preserved.
